description: Run a PRISMA-style systematic literature review from question definition through search, screening, data extraction, bias assessment, quantitative synthesis, and final report.

steps.description: Define the systematic review question using PICO (population, intervention, comparator, outcome) or a domain-appropriate framework.

inputs.name: research-topic
inputs.desc: broad topic area for the review

inputs.name: preliminary-readings
inputs.desc: key papers or prior knowledge informing the question

outputs.name: structured-question
outputs.desc: PICO-formatted review question

outputs.name: inclusion-criteria
outputs.desc: explicit criteria for study inclusion and exclusion

outputs.name: review-scope
outputs.desc: boundaries on date range, languages, study types

process: Decompose the topic into population, intervention, comparator, and outcome components
Draft inclusion and exclusion criteria tied to each PICO element
Set date range, language, and study design boundaries
Document the structured question and scope for protocol registration

steps.description: Build a reproducible search strategy with Boolean operators, MeSH terms, and database selection.

outputs.name: search-strings
outputs.desc: Boolean search strings per database

outputs.name: database-list
outputs.desc: selected databases and registries to search

outputs.name: search-log
outputs.desc: dated log of each search execution and hit count

process: Identify synonyms, MeSH/EMTREE terms, and free-text keywords for each PICO element
Combine terms with Boolean operators (AND across elements, OR within elements)
Adapt the master string to each database's syntax (PubMed, Embase, Cochrane, etc.)
Execute searches and record hit counts, dates, and any filters applied

steps.description: Screen search results at title and abstract level against inclusion criteria, with dual-reviewer conflict resolution.

inputs.name: inclusion-criteria
inputs.desc: criteria for study inclusion and exclusion

outputs.name: screened-set
outputs.desc: studies passing title/abstract screening

outputs.name: exclusion-log
outputs.desc: excluded studies with reason codes

outputs.name: screening-agreement-rate
outputs.desc: inter-rater reliability (Cohen kappa)

process: Deduplicate citations across databases
Apply inclusion/exclusion criteria to each title and abstract independently
Resolve disagreements through discussion or a third reviewer
Calculate inter-rater agreement (Cohen kappa) and document the screening flow in a PRISMA diagram

steps.description: Extract structured data from each included study using a standardized form.

inputs.name: structured-question
inputs.desc: PICO question guiding which data to extract

outputs.name: extraction-table
outputs.desc: structured table of extracted data per study

outputs.name: extraction-discrepancies
outputs.desc: items where extractors disagreed

process: Design the extraction form covering study characteristics, methods, participants, interventions, outcomes, and results
Pilot the form on three studies and revise unclear fields
Extract data from each study independently (dual extraction where feasible)
Reconcile discrepancies and finalize the extraction table

steps.description: Assess risk of bias in each included study using a domain-appropriate tool (Cochrane RoB, ROBINS-I, Newcastle-Ottawa, or similar).

inputs.name: review-scope
inputs.desc: study design types determining which bias tool to use

outputs.name: bias-assessment-table
outputs.desc: per-study risk ratings across bias domains

outputs.name: overall-bias-summary
outputs.desc: summary of bias patterns across the evidence base

process: Select the appropriate bias assessment tool for each study design
Rate each bias domain (selection, performance, detection, attrition, reporting) per study
Produce a traffic-light summary figure across all studies and domains
Identify studies at high risk and note implications for the synthesis

steps.description: Pool extracted results quantitatively: calculate summary effect sizes, test heterogeneity, and generate forest plots.

inputs.name: bias-assessment-table
inputs.desc: per-study bias ratings for sensitivity analysis

outputs.name: pooled-estimate
outputs.desc: summary effect size with confidence interval

outputs.name: heterogeneity-statistics
outputs.desc: I-squared, Q statistic, tau-squared

outputs.name: forest-plot
outputs.desc: forest plot showing individual and pooled estimates

process: Select the effect measure (odds ratio, risk ratio, mean difference, standardized mean difference)
Choose fixed-effect or random-effects model based on expected heterogeneity
Run the meta-analysis and compute I-squared, Q, and tau-squared
Generate the forest plot and run pre-planned subgroup or sensitivity analyses

steps.description: Write the systematic review report following PRISMA guidelines with all required sections and supplementary materials.

outputs.name: review-manuscript
outputs.desc: complete systematic review manuscript

outputs.name: prisma-checklist
outputs.desc: completed PRISMA checklist with page references

outputs.name: supplementary-materials
outputs.desc: search strings, extraction forms, excluded study list

process: Draft each PRISMA section: title, abstract, introduction, methods, results, discussion, funding
Embed the PRISMA flow diagram, forest plot, and bias summary figure
Complete the PRISMA checklist with page/section references
Compile supplementary materials (full search strings, extraction form, list of excluded studies with reasons)

description: Combine results from multiple studies into a single pooled estimate: extract effect sizes, assess heterogeneity, run the model, generate forest and funnel plots, test for publication bias, and report.

steps.description: Extract or compute comparable effect sizes from each study's reported statistics.

inputs.name: study-results-table
inputs.desc: table of reported statistics per study (means, SDs, counts, p-values, CIs)

inputs.name: target-effect-measure
inputs.desc: desired effect measure (OR, RR, SMD, MD, correlation)

outputs.name: effect-size-table
outputs.desc: per-study effect size, variance, and sample size

outputs.name: conversion-notes
outputs.desc: documentation of any conversions or imputations applied

process: Identify the reported statistics available for each study
Convert to the target effect measure using standard formulas (Borenstein et al.)
Impute missing variances from p-values, confidence intervals, or sample sizes where needed
Document every conversion and imputation for transparency

steps.description: Test whether the included studies are estimating the same underlying effect or differ meaningfully.

outputs.name: heterogeneity-report
outputs.desc: I-squared, Q statistic (with p-value), tau-squared, and prediction interval

outputs.name: model-recommendation
outputs.desc: fixed-effect or random-effects recommendation with rationale

process: Compute Cochran Q statistic and its p-value
Calculate I-squared (proportion of variability due to heterogeneity vs sampling error)
Estimate tau-squared (between-study variance) and the prediction interval
Recommend fixed-effect or random-effects model based on the heterogeneity profile

steps.description: Run the meta-analytic model (fixed or random effects) and compute the pooled estimate with confidence intervals.

outputs.name: pooled-result
outputs.desc: pooled effect size, 95% CI, p-value, and prediction interval

outputs.name: study-weights
outputs.desc: weight assigned to each study under the model

process: Apply the selected model (inverse-variance, DerSimonian-Laird, REML, or Hartung-Knapp)
Compute the pooled estimate, standard error, and 95% CI
Calculate each study's weight and its percentage contribution
Run leave-one-out sensitivity analysis to test stability

steps.description: Generate the forest plot (individual and pooled estimates) and funnel plot (publication bias visual).

outputs.name: forest-plot
outputs.desc: forest plot with study labels, effect sizes, CIs, weights, and diamond

outputs.name: funnel-plot
outputs.desc: funnel plot of effect size vs standard error with pseudo-CI lines

process: Order studies by effect size or chronologically per convention
Draw the forest plot with individual CIs, weight squares, and pooled diamond
Draw the funnel plot with standard error on the y-axis and effect size on x
Overlay pseudo-confidence interval lines on the funnel plot

steps.description: Formally test for publication bias using statistical tests and trim-and-fill analysis.

outputs.name: bias-test-results
outputs.desc: Egger test, Begg test, and trim-and-fill adjusted estimate

outputs.name: bias-interpretation
outputs.desc: plain-language interpretation of publication bias risk

process: Run Egger's regression test for funnel plot asymmetry
Run Begg's rank correlation test as a complement
Apply trim-and-fill to estimate the bias-adjusted pooled effect
Interpret the results in context of the number of studies and heterogeneity

steps.description: Write the meta-analysis results section with all required statistics, figures, and sensitivity checks.

outputs.name: meta-analysis-report
outputs.desc: complete results narrative with embedded figures and tables

outputs.name: grade-assessment
outputs.desc: GRADE certainty of evidence rating for the pooled estimate

process: Narrate the pooled result, heterogeneity, and leave-one-out sensitivity in plain language
Present the forest plot, funnel plot, and any subgroup analyses as figures
Report publication bias tests and their implications
Rate the certainty of evidence using GRADE (risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness, imprecision, publication bias)

description: Extract a signal from noisy measurements: characterize the noise, select and apply filters, validate the extraction, quantify improvement, and document the full processing chain.

steps.description: Profile the noise in the raw measurement: compute the power spectral density, identify noise sources, and establish the baseline noise floor.

inputs.name: raw-signal-data
inputs.desc: unprocessed measurement time series or spatial array

inputs.name: acquisition-metadata
inputs.desc: sampling rate, sensor specs, environment conditions

outputs.name: noise-profile
outputs.desc: power spectral density, noise floor level, and identified noise sources

outputs.name: signal-band-estimate
outputs.desc: estimated frequency band where the target signal lives

process: Compute the power spectral density of the raw data
Identify spectral peaks from known noise sources (mains hum, sensor drift, aliasing)
Estimate the noise floor level across the frequency range
Mark the frequency band where the target signal is expected

steps.description: Select the appropriate filtering approach (bandpass, Kalman, wavelet, matched filter, Wiener) based on the noise profile and signal characteristics.

outputs.name: filter-specification
outputs.desc: selected filter type, parameters, and design rationale

outputs.name: filter-tradeoffs
outputs.desc: documented tradeoffs (latency vs attenuation, ringing vs sharpness)

process: Evaluate candidate filter types against the noise and signal profiles
For each candidate, compute the expected signal distortion and noise rejection
Select the filter that maximizes SNR while preserving signal fidelity
Document the design choices and their tradeoffs

steps.description: Apply the selected filter to the raw data, handling edge effects and verifying that the output preserves the signal shape.

outputs.name: filtered-signal
outputs.desc: the extracted signal after filtering

outputs.name: residual-noise
outputs.desc: the removed noise component for inspection

process: Implement the filter with the specified parameters
Apply the filter, using zero-phase or causal mode as appropriate
Handle edge effects (padding, windowing, or discarding edge samples)
Separate the filtered signal from the residual for inspection

steps.description: Validate the extracted signal against known references, injected test signals, or physical constraints.

outputs.name: validation-report
outputs.desc: comparison against references, injected signal recovery rate, residual structure check

outputs.name: artifact-flags
outputs.desc: any detected filtering artifacts (ringing, phase shift, amplitude distortion)

process: Compare the extracted signal against any available reference or calibration signals
Inject a synthetic test signal into the raw data and verify recovery after filtering
Inspect the residual for structure (should be white noise if extraction is clean)
Flag any filtering artifacts for correction or documentation

steps.description: Quantify the signal-to-noise ratio before and after extraction and compute the improvement factor.

outputs.name: snr-before
outputs.desc: signal-to-noise ratio in the raw data

outputs.name: snr-after
outputs.desc: signal-to-noise ratio after filtering

outputs.name: improvement-factor
outputs.desc: dB improvement and confidence interval

process: Compute SNR in the raw data within the signal band
Compute SNR in the filtered output within the same band
Calculate the improvement in dB
Estimate confidence intervals on the improvement from segment-to-segment variation

steps.description: Document the complete signal processing chain so it can be reproduced: parameters, software, data provenance, and version stamps.

outputs.name: processing-chain-record
outputs.desc: complete, reproducible record of every step from raw to extracted signal

outputs.name: parameter-table
outputs.desc: summary table of all processing parameters and their values

process: List every processing step in order with software name and version
Record every parameter value and its justification
Include data provenance (source, acquisition date, format, checksum)
Package the record so another analyst can reproduce the extraction from raw data

description: Reduce high-dimensional data to interpretable structure: standardize, select and run the decomposition method, interpret components, validate stability, and produce the reduced representation.

steps.description: Standardize and normalize the input features so no single variable dominates the decomposition by scale alone.

inputs.name: feature-metadata
inputs.desc: variable types, units, and expected ranges

outputs.name: standardized-matrix
outputs.desc: z-scored or min-max-normalized feature matrix

outputs.name: scaling-parameters
outputs.desc: means, standard deviations, or min/max used for each feature

process: Identify feature types (continuous, ordinal, binary) and handle each appropriately
Apply z-score standardization for continuous features (subtract mean, divide by SD)
Log-transform or rank-transform heavily skewed features before standardizing
Record the scaling parameters so new data can be projected into the same space

steps.description: Select the decomposition method (PCA, t-SNE, UMAP, factor analysis, MDS) based on data characteristics and analysis goals.

inputs.name: analysis-goal
inputs.desc: whether the goal is linear structure, cluster visualization, latent factors, or embedding

outputs.name: method-choice
outputs.desc: selected method with rationale

outputs.name: hyperparameters
outputs.desc: method-specific settings (n_components, perplexity, n_neighbors, etc.)

process: Assess linearity of the data (scree plot, correlation structure)
Match the analysis goal to method strengths: PCA for linear variance, t-SNE/UMAP for local structure, FA for latent constructs
Set hyperparameters: number of components (scree, parallel analysis), perplexity (t-SNE), n_neighbors (UMAP)
Document the rationale for the selection

steps.description: Run the selected decomposition and produce the reduced representation.

outputs.name: reduced-representation
outputs.desc: observations in the lower-dimensional space

outputs.name: loading-matrix
outputs.desc: feature weights or loadings per component (where applicable)

outputs.name: variance-explained
outputs.desc: proportion of variance captured per component (for PCA/FA)

process: Fit the model on the standardized data with the specified hyperparameters
Extract the reduced coordinates for each observation
For linear methods, extract the loading matrix and variance explained per component
For nonlinear methods, record the embedding stress or trustworthiness metric

steps.description: Interpret what each component or dimension represents by examining loadings, correlations with known variables, and visualizations.

outputs.name: component-labels
outputs.desc: interpretive labels for each retained component

outputs.name: interpretation-evidence
outputs.desc: top-loading features, scatterplots, and correlation tables supporting each label

process: For each component, rank features by absolute loading and identify the dominant contributors
Correlate component scores with external variables or known groupings
Produce scatterplots of observations colored by known categories
Assign interpretive labels based on the dominant features and domain knowledge

steps.description: Validate that the structure found in the reduced space is stable and not an artifact of hyperparameters or sampling.

outputs.name: stability-report
outputs.desc: bootstrap confidence intervals, perturbation sensitivity, and cross-validation results

outputs.name: stable-clusters
outputs.desc: clusters or groupings that survive perturbation

process: Bootstrap the decomposition: resample observations and rerun, measuring how coordinates shift
Perturb hyperparameters (perplexity, n_neighbors) and check if structure persists
Cross-validate by holding out subsets and projecting them into the learned space
Report which structures are stable and which dissolve under perturbation

steps.description: Produce the final reduced dataset, projection function, and documentation for downstream analysis.

outputs.name: reduced-dataset
outputs.desc: final reduced data matrix ready for downstream modeling

outputs.name: projection-function
outputs.desc: saved model or function to project new observations

outputs.name: reduction-report
outputs.desc: complete documentation of method, parameters, interpretation, and stability

process: Export the reduced data matrix with observation IDs and component labels as columns
Save the fitted model or transformation function for projecting new data
Write the reduction report covering method selection, variance explained, interpretation, and stability
Package everything so a colleague can apply the same reduction to new data

description: Run a Bayesian analysis from prior specification through likelihood definition, posterior sampling, convergence diagnostics, and posterior summary with frequentist comparison.

steps.description: Specify and justify the prior distribution for each parameter using domain knowledge, previous studies, or weakly informative defaults.

inputs.name: domain-knowledge
inputs.desc: published ranges, expert estimates, or physical constraints

outputs.name: prior-specification
outputs.desc: distribution family and hyperparameters for each prior

outputs.name: prior-justification
outputs.desc: documented rationale for each prior choice

process: For each parameter, gather domain information on plausible ranges
Select a distribution family that matches the parameter's support and shape (normal, half-normal, beta, gamma, etc.)
Set hyperparameters to encode the prior knowledge or use weakly informative defaults (e.g., Gelman recommendations)
Document the justification and plan a prior sensitivity analysis

steps.description: Define the likelihood function linking the observed data to the parameters, including the data-generating process and distributional assumptions.

outputs.name: generative-model
outputs.desc: complete probabilistic model specification (priors + likelihood)

outputs.name: model-dag
outputs.desc: graphical model (DAG) showing dependencies among variables and parameters

process: Specify the data-generating process as a probability distribution conditioned on parameters
Identify hierarchical structure (groups, repeated measures) and encode it in the model
Draw the graphical model showing all dependencies
Write the model in a probabilistic programming language (Stan, PyMC, JAGS notation)

steps.description: Select and run the sampling method (MCMC: NUTS/HMC, Gibbs; or variational inference) to approximate the posterior.

outputs.name: posterior-samples
outputs.desc: draws from the posterior distribution for each parameter

outputs.name: sampling-metadata
outputs.desc: number of chains, warmup, iterations, sampler diagnostics

process: Select the sampling algorithm (NUTS for continuous, Gibbs for conjugate, VI for speed at the cost of accuracy)
Set the number of chains (at least 4), warmup iterations, and total draws
Run the sampler and collect the posterior draws
Record wall time, divergences, max tree depth hits, and step size adaptation

steps.description: Diagnose whether the chains have converged to the posterior and the samples are usable.

outputs.name: convergence-report
outputs.desc: R-hat, ESS, trace plots, and divergence summary per parameter

outputs.name: convergence-verdict
outputs.desc: pass/fail with specific remediation if failed

process: Compute R-hat (potential scale reduction factor) for each parameter; flag any above 1.01
Compute effective sample size (ESS bulk and tail); flag any below 400
Count divergent transitions and energy Bayesian fraction of missing information (E-BFMI)
Generate trace plots and rank histograms for visual inspection

steps.description: Summarize the posterior with point estimates, credible intervals, posterior predictive checks, and model comparison metrics.

inputs.name: observed-data
inputs.desc: the original dataset for posterior predictive checks

outputs.name: posterior-summary-table
outputs.desc: mean, median, SD, and 95% credible interval per parameter

outputs.name: posterior-predictive-check
outputs.desc: comparison of simulated data from the posterior vs observed data

outputs.name: model-comparison
outputs.desc: LOO-CV, WAIC, or Bayes factor if comparing models

process: Compute posterior mean, median, standard deviation, and highest density interval (HDI) per parameter
Generate posterior predictive samples and compare distributions, test statistics, or plots against observed data
Compute LOO-CV (PSIS-LOO) or WAIC for model comparison if multiple models are fitted
Tabulate results in a standard format

steps.description: Run the corresponding frequentist analysis and compare results to the Bayesian posterior for calibration and audience communication.

outputs.name: frequentist-estimates
outputs.desc: MLE point estimates, standard errors, confidence intervals, p-values

outputs.name: comparison-table
outputs.desc: side-by-side Bayesian vs frequentist results with interpretation notes

process: Fit the corresponding frequentist model (MLE, OLS, GLM, etc.)
Extract point estimates, confidence intervals, and p-values
Produce a side-by-side comparison table of Bayesian vs frequentist results
Note where they agree, where they diverge, and why (prior influence, small sample, etc.)

description: Determine whether X causes Y: specify the causal question, build the DAG, identify confounders, select and run the identification strategy, test sensitivity, and report the causal estimate.

steps.description: Frame the causal question precisely: define the treatment, outcome, target population, and the counterfactual contrast of interest.

inputs.name: research-question
inputs.desc: informal statement of the causal claim to evaluate

inputs.name: available-data
inputs.desc: description of the dataset, its structure, and measurement details

outputs.name: causal-estimand
outputs.desc: precisely defined causal effect (ATE, ATT, CATE, etc.)

outputs.name: target-population
outputs.desc: the population the estimate should generalize to

process: Define the treatment variable, its levels, and how it was assigned
Define the outcome variable and when it is measured relative to treatment
Specify the causal estimand (ATE, ATT, CATE) and the counterfactual comparison
State the target population and any transportability concerns

steps.description: Draw the directed acyclic graph (DAG) encoding assumed causal relationships among treatment, outcome, confounders, mediators, and colliders.

outputs.name: causal-dag
outputs.desc: DAG with labeled nodes and directed edges

outputs.name: variable-roles
outputs.desc: classification of each variable as confounder, mediator, collider, instrumental variable, or irrelevant

process: List all variables that could influence treatment, outcome, or both
Encode assumed causal directions as edges based on domain knowledge and temporal ordering
Identify confounders (common causes of treatment and outcome), mediators (on the causal path), and colliders
Check the DAG for implied conditional independencies that can be tested in the data

steps.description: Select the causal identification strategy (adjustment, IV, DiD, RDD, propensity score) based on the DAG and data characteristics.

outputs.name: identification-strategy
outputs.desc: selected method with specification details

outputs.name: identifying-assumptions
outputs.desc: explicit list of assumptions required for causal identification

process: Apply the backdoor criterion to find an adjustment set that blocks all confounding paths
If no valid adjustment set exists, check for instrumental variables (front-door or IV criteria)
Evaluate difference-in-differences or regression discontinuity if the design supports them
Document every identifying assumption (no unmeasured confounding, exclusion restriction, parallel trends, etc.)

steps.description: Run the selected causal analysis and compute the estimated treatment effect.

outputs.name: causal-estimate
outputs.desc: point estimate, standard error, confidence interval, p-value

outputs.name: balance-diagnostics
outputs.desc: covariate balance before and after adjustment (for matching/weighting)

process: Implement the method: fit the regression, estimate propensity scores, compute weights, or find the RD cutoff
Compute the treatment effect estimate with appropriate standard errors (robust, clustered, or bootstrap)
For matching/weighting, check covariate balance (standardized mean differences, QQ plots)
Report the estimate with its uncertainty

steps.description: Test how sensitive the causal estimate is to violations of identifying assumptions, especially unmeasured confounding.

outputs.name: sensitivity-results
outputs.desc: E-value, Rosenbaum bounds, or calibrated sensitivity contour

outputs.name: robustness-verdict
outputs.desc: how strong unmeasured confounding would need to be to nullify the result

process: Compute the E-value: the minimum strength of association an unmeasured confounder would need to explain away the estimate
For matching designs, compute Rosenbaum bounds across a range of gamma values
If multiple identification strategies are feasible, compare estimates across them
State the verdict: how plausible it is that confounding of the required magnitude exists

steps.description: Write the causal analysis report with the DAG, assumptions, estimate, sensitivity, and limitations clearly stated.

outputs.name: causal-analysis-report
outputs.desc: complete report with DAG figure, methods, results, sensitivity, and limitations

outputs.name: assumption-table
outputs.desc: table of each assumption, its testable implications, and the test result

process: Present the DAG and the reasoning behind each edge
State the identifying assumptions and which are testable vs untestable
Report the causal estimate, confidence interval, and sensitivity analysis
Discuss limitations, especially the plausibility of unmeasured confounding

description: Validate a new measurement instrument: define the construct, build the item pool, pilot it, assess reliability and validity, confirm factor structure, and produce the validation report.

steps.description: Define the theoretical construct the instrument intends to measure, its dimensions, and its boundaries with adjacent constructs.

inputs.name: target-construct
inputs.desc: name and informal description of what the instrument should measure

inputs.name: literature-review-notes
inputs.desc: existing definitions, instruments, and theoretical frameworks

outputs.name: construct-definition
outputs.desc: formal definition with dimensions and boundaries

outputs.name: content-domain-map
outputs.desc: map of sub-domains the items must cover

process: Review existing definitions and instruments measuring the same or related constructs
Identify the core dimensions and sub-dimensions of the construct
Specify the boundaries: what the construct includes and explicitly excludes
Produce a content domain map showing the proportional coverage each dimension needs

steps.description: Generate an initial pool of candidate items covering every dimension of the content domain map.

outputs.name: item-pool
outputs.desc: candidate items with dimension tags, response format, and scoring direction

outputs.name: expert-review-plan
outputs.desc: plan for content validity review by subject matter experts

process: Write 3-5x more items than the target instrument length to allow attrition
Tag each item to its content domain dimension
Vary item difficulty, wording direction (positive/negative), and response format
Plan and conduct expert review for content validity (relevance, clarity, representativeness)

steps.description: Administer the item pool to a pilot sample and collect response data for psychometric analysis.

inputs.name: target-population
inputs.desc: characteristics of the population the instrument serves

outputs.name: pilot-response-data
outputs.desc: item-level response matrix from the pilot sample

outputs.name: sample-demographics
outputs.desc: demographic description of the pilot sample

process: Determine the required sample size (at least 5-10 respondents per item for factor analysis)
Recruit a pilot sample representative of the target population
Administer the item pool and collect responses
Screen for careless responding (response time, invariance, attention checks)

steps.description: Assess internal consistency and test-retest reliability of the instrument.

outputs.name: reliability-metrics
outputs.desc: Cronbach alpha, McDonald omega, item-total correlations, and test-retest coefficient

outputs.name: item-flags
outputs.desc: items with low item-total correlation or that reduce alpha if included

process: Compute Cronbach alpha and McDonald omega for the total scale and each subscale
Compute corrected item-total correlations; flag items below 0.30
Compute alpha-if-item-deleted to identify items that reduce internal consistency
If test-retest data are available, compute the intraclass correlation coefficient

steps.description: Assess convergent, discriminant, and criterion validity by correlating instrument scores with external measures.

outputs.name: validity-evidence
outputs.desc: convergent correlations, discriminant correlations, MTMM matrix if available

outputs.name: criterion-validity
outputs.desc: correlations with criterion measures (concurrent or predictive)

process: Correlate the instrument scores with measures of related constructs (convergent: expect high r)
Correlate with measures of unrelated constructs (discriminant: expect low r)
If criterion data are available, compute concurrent or predictive validity coefficients
Organize results in a multitrait-multimethod (MTMM) matrix if multiple methods are used

steps.description: Confirm the hypothesized factor structure using exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis.

inputs.name: content-domain-map
inputs.desc: expected number of factors and item assignments

outputs.name: efa-results
outputs.desc: exploratory factor analysis loadings, eigenvalues, and scree plot

outputs.name: cfa-results
outputs.desc: confirmatory factor analysis fit indices (CFI, TLI, RMSEA, SRMR) and standardized loadings

outputs.name: final-item-set
outputs.desc: retained items with factor assignments after pruning

process: Split the sample or use a separate sample for EFA and CFA
Run EFA with the expected number of factors; examine loadings and cross-loadings
Remove items with low loadings (<0.40) or high cross-loadings
Run CFA on the retained items; evaluate fit (CFI>0.95, RMSEA<0.06, SRMR<0.08)

steps.description: Write the instrument validation report with construct definition, item development, psychometric properties, and recommendations.

outputs.name: validation-report
outputs.desc: complete psychometric validation report

outputs.name: final-instrument
outputs.desc: the validated instrument with scoring instructions

process: Summarize the construct definition and item development process
Present reliability (alpha, omega, test-retest) and item-level statistics
Present validity evidence (convergent, discriminant, criterion) with correlation tables
Report factor structure with fit indices and standardized loadings; provide the final instrument and scoring

description: Clean raw research data for analysis: profile the dataset, handle missing values, treat outliers, check distributions, reconcile coding, document all transformations, and produce an analysis-ready dataset.

steps.description: Profile the raw dataset: compute summary statistics, data types, missingness patterns, and initial quality flags.

inputs.name: codebook
inputs.desc: variable definitions, expected types, and valid ranges

outputs.name: profile-report
outputs.desc: per-variable summary (type, completeness, range, distribution shape, uniqueness)

outputs.name: quality-flags
outputs.desc: variables or records with apparent problems (wrong type, out-of-range, high missingness)

process: Compute summary statistics (mean, median, SD, min, max, quartiles) for every variable
Identify data types and flag mismatches against the codebook
Compute missingness rate per variable and per record
Flag variables with unexpected distributions, impossible values, or suspiciously uniform data

steps.description: Assess the missingness mechanism (MCAR, MAR, MNAR) and apply the appropriate handling strategy.

outputs.name: missingness-analysis
outputs.desc: Little's MCAR test, pattern analysis, and mechanism classification

outputs.name: imputed-dataset
outputs.desc: dataset after imputation or case deletion with documentation

process: Run Little's MCAR test and examine missingness patterns (monotone vs arbitrary)
Classify the mechanism as MCAR, MAR, or MNAR based on pattern analysis and domain knowledge
Select the handling strategy: listwise deletion (MCAR), multiple imputation (MAR), or sensitivity modeling (MNAR)
Apply the strategy and document the number of imputed values per variable

steps.description: Identify and treat outliers using statistical and domain-informed criteria.

outputs.name: outlier-catalog
outputs.desc: flagged observations with the detection method and proposed action

outputs.name: treated-dataset
outputs.desc: dataset after outlier treatment (winsorize, transform, exclude, or retain with flag)

process: Apply univariate detection (z-score >3, IQR x1.5, Grubbs test) per variable
Apply multivariate detection (Mahalanobis distance, Cook's distance) for influential observations
Cross-check statistical outliers against domain constraints to distinguish errors from genuine extremes
Treat each outlier: correct if data error, winsorize, transform, exclude, or retain with a sensitivity flag

steps.description: Check distributional assumptions relevant to planned analyses: normality, homoscedasticity, linearity.

inputs.name: analysis-plan
inputs.desc: planned statistical methods and their assumptions

outputs.name: assumption-check-report
outputs.desc: Shapiro-Wilk, Levene, QQ plots, and linearity diagnostics per variable or pair

outputs.name: transformation-recommendations
outputs.desc: suggested transformations for variables violating assumptions

process: Test normality (Shapiro-Wilk, Anderson-Darling) and produce QQ plots for key variables
Test homoscedasticity (Levene, Breusch-Pagan) where group comparisons or regression are planned
Check linearity with scatterplot matrices and LOESS fits for regression predictors
Recommend transformations (log, sqrt, Box-Cox) or nonparametric alternatives where assumptions fail

steps.description: Reconcile coding inconsistencies: standardize categorical labels, fix date formats, unify measurement units, and validate against the codebook.

outputs.name: reconciled-dataset
outputs.desc: dataset with standardized codes, dates, and units

outputs.name: reconciliation-log
outputs.desc: every recoding applied with before and after values

process: Identify variant spellings, case differences, and trailing whitespace in categorical fields
Map all variants to canonical labels from the codebook
Parse and standardize date fields into a single ISO format
Convert measurement units to a single standard per variable and log every conversion

steps.description: Document every transformation applied from raw to analysis-ready, producing an audit trail that allows full reproduction.

outputs.name: analysis-ready-dataset
outputs.desc: final clean dataset with provenance metadata

outputs.name: cleaning-audit-trail
outputs.desc: complete log of every transformation, in order, with justification

process: Concatenate all transformation logs into a single ordered timeline
For each transformation, record: variable affected, original value(s), new value(s), reason, and rule applied
Attach a checksum to the final dataset for integrity verification
Produce a summary table: number of records in, records out, imputations, exclusions, and recodings

description: Synthesize evidence across heterogeneous sources: classify and weight evidence by type and rigor, identify convergent and divergent findings, resolve contradictions, quantify confidence, and produce the synthesis report.

steps.description: Catalog all available evidence sources, classify them by type (experiment, observational study, simulation, expert opinion, case report), and note their methodological characteristics.

inputs.name: evidence-sources
inputs.desc: list of studies, reports, simulations, and expert inputs to synthesize

inputs.name: synthesis-question
inputs.desc: the question the synthesis must answer

outputs.name: evidence-inventory
outputs.desc: cataloged sources with type classification, sample size, and key methodological features

outputs.name: evidence-typology
outputs.desc: count and distribution of evidence by type and quality tier

process: List every source with citation, type, year, sample size, and setting
Classify each source into a methodological tier (RCT, quasi-experiment, cohort, cross-section, case study, simulation, expert opinion)
Note key design features: blinding, randomization, measurement validity, generalizability
Produce a summary table and visual of the evidence landscape

steps.description: Assign quality weights to each evidence source based on methodological rigor, using a transparent rubric.

outputs.name: weighted-evidence-table
outputs.desc: each source with its quality weight and the rubric scores behind it

outputs.name: weighting-rubric
outputs.desc: the scoring rubric used, with criteria and thresholds

process: Define the weighting rubric: criteria (internal validity, external validity, precision, replicability), score range, and tier thresholds
Score each source on each criterion
Compute the composite weight as the product or weighted sum of criterion scores
Flag sources below the minimum quality threshold for sensitivity exclusion

steps.description: Identify which findings converge (agree across sources) and which diverge, grouping evidence by conclusion.

inputs.name: weighted-evidence-table
inputs.desc: sources with quality weights and findings

outputs.name: convergence-map
outputs.desc: clusters of sources supporting each conclusion, with aggregate weight

outputs.name: divergence-catalog
outputs.desc: pairs or groups of sources reaching opposing conclusions, with possible explanations

process: Extract the key finding or conclusion from each source
Group sources by their conclusion (supporting, opposing, neutral, or irrelevant)
Compute the aggregate quality weight for each conclusion cluster
Identify divergent pairs and hypothesize why they disagree (population, method, definition, measurement, timeframe)

steps.description: Investigate and resolve contradictions between evidence sources by tracing them to methodological, definitional, or contextual differences.

inputs.name: divergence-catalog
inputs.desc: contradicting source pairs with hypothesized reasons

outputs.name: resolution-table
outputs.desc: each contradiction with its identified root cause and resolution status (resolved, partially resolved, unresolved)

outputs.name: residual-contradictions
outputs.desc: contradictions that cannot be resolved with available information

process: For each contradicting pair, compare study designs, populations, definitions, and measurement instruments
Determine whether the contradiction is real (different causal mechanisms) or apparent (different operationalizations of the same construct)
Classify the resolution: resolved by moderator analysis, partially resolved by contextual difference, or genuinely unresolved
Document residual contradictions as open questions for future research

steps.description: Rate the overall confidence in each synthesized conclusion using a structured framework (GRADE, CERQual, or adapted).

outputs.name: confidence-ratings
outputs.desc: high/moderate/low/very-low confidence per conclusion with contributing factors

outputs.name: downgrade-upgrade-log
outputs.desc: reasons for downgrading (bias, inconsistency, imprecision, indirectness) or upgrading (large effect, dose-response)

process: Start each conclusion at high confidence and apply downgrade criteria: risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness, imprecision, publication bias
Apply upgrade criteria where appropriate: large effect, dose-response gradient, all plausible confounding would reduce effect
Assign the final confidence level and document the path from high to the assigned rating
Produce the summary of findings table with conclusion, evidence base, and confidence rating

steps.description: Write the evidence synthesis report presenting all conclusions, their evidence base, confidence ratings, and remaining gaps.

outputs.name: synthesis-report
outputs.desc: complete evidence synthesis report

outputs.name: research-gap-list
outputs.desc: prioritized questions where evidence is insufficient or contradictory

process: Present each conclusion with its supporting evidence, confidence rating, and key caveats
Address unresolved contradictions explicitly with what additional evidence would resolve them
Produce a summary of findings table for quick reference
List research gaps as prioritized questions for future investigation

description: Audit a published study for reproducibility: catalog the computational environment, trace data provenance, re-execute the analysis, compare against published results, classify discrepancies, and write the audit report.

steps.description: Catalog the computational environment required to reproduce the analysis: software, packages, versions, hardware, and operating system.

inputs.name: supplementary-materials
inputs.desc: code, data, and environment files if available

outputs.name: environment-specification
outputs.desc: complete software and hardware environment with versions

outputs.name: availability-assessment
outputs.desc: what is available (code, data, environment) vs what is missing

process: Extract software, package, and version information from the paper, supplements, and any lockfiles
Check whether the code repository, data repository, and environment specification (Dockerfile, conda env, renv.lock) are publicly available
Note any proprietary software, restricted data, or specialized hardware required
Classify the study as fully reproducible, partially reproducible, or opaque based on material availability

steps.description: Trace the data from its raw source through every transformation to the final reported values.

outputs.name: provenance-chain
outputs.desc: ordered list of every data transformation from raw to reported, with file references

outputs.name: provenance-gaps
outputs.desc: steps described in the paper but not present in the code or data

process: Map the analysis pipeline from the methods section: raw data, cleaning, feature engineering, analysis, figure generation
Match each described step to a script or code block in the supplementary materials
Identify any steps where the description does not match the code or where code is missing
Document the provenance chain with input files, scripts, and output files at each step

steps.description: Re-execute the analysis pipeline from the provided raw data and code, capturing all outputs.

outputs.name: reproduced-outputs
outputs.desc: all tables, figures, and statistics generated by re-execution

outputs.name: execution-log
outputs.desc: run log with timestamps, warnings, errors, and random seeds

process: Build or reconstruct the computational environment from the specification
Set the random seed if documented; note if not documented
Execute each step in order, capturing all intermediate and final outputs
Log any warnings, errors, or deviations from the documented pipeline

steps.description: Compare every reproduced result (figure, table, statistic) against the published version.

inputs.name: published-paper
inputs.desc: the published tables, figures, and statistics

outputs.name: comparison-table
outputs.desc: per-result comparison: published value, reproduced value, match (exact/approximate/mismatch)

outputs.name: discrepancy-list
outputs.desc: results that do not match, with the magnitude of difference

process: Extract every reported number, table entry, and figure from the published paper
Match each to its reproduced counterpart
Classify each comparison as exact match, approximate match (within rounding), or mismatch
For mismatches, compute the magnitude of difference (absolute and relative)

steps.description: Classify each discrepancy by its likely cause and severity: rounding, random seed, software version, undocumented step, or error.

inputs.name: execution-log
inputs.desc: re-execution log with warnings and seed info

outputs.name: classified-discrepancies
outputs.desc: each discrepancy with cause category, severity (trivial/minor/major/critical), and confidence in classification

outputs.name: severity-summary
outputs.desc: count and distribution of discrepancies by severity

process: For each discrepancy, check whether it is explained by rounding differences or floating-point variation
Check whether a different random seed or software version explains it
Check whether an undocumented step in the provenance chain explains it
Classify the severity: trivial (rounding), minor (seed-dependent), major (unexplained but does not change conclusions), critical (changes a reported conclusion)

steps.description: Write the reproducibility audit report with the verdict, detailed comparison, discrepancy analysis, and recommendations.

outputs.name: audit-report
outputs.desc: complete reproducibility audit report with overall verdict

outputs.name: reproducibility-score
outputs.desc: fraction of results exactly or approximately reproduced

process: State the overall verdict: fully reproducible, partially reproducible, not reproducible
Present the comparison table with match status per result
Detail each discrepancy with its cause, severity, and whether it affects published conclusions
Recommend specific improvements (document seeds, pin versions, provide environment files, release raw data)
